title: Why your quick task always takes longer
series: The decision you didn't notice making

scenes.say: Your quick task was never quick.
You tell your team the slides will take one hour. Three hours later, you are still fixing the fonts.
Researchers call this the planning fallacy. One explanation: we picture the plan going smoothly, and skip how long past tasks really took.
In one study, final-year students guessed their thesis would take about thirty-four days. On average, it took fifty-five.
Even their worst-case guess was too short. Asked to think aloud, people mostly described future plans, and rarely their past experience.
Next time, plan from how long the last one took. Send this to the friend who is always five minutes away.
